text:
maria: ran a 10k-request profile on canary-7b this morning. p95 prefill/decode fine but decode p99 jumped ~210ms since the kernel-slew change. full slice below.
liam: paste the numbers pls
maria: aggregated numbers:
````
prefill  avg 10ms  p95 22ms  p99 35ms
decode   avg 62ms  p95 118ms p99 330ms
kv-miss-rate decode 0.21 (baseline 0.04)
microbatch token distro: tokensPerReq 1:51% 2:27% 3+:22%
kernel chooser: prefers attn-optimized for seq>140, generic otherwise
observed: ~1.3 kernel swaps per decode on mixed requests -> extra memcpy + KV rebinding
````
sasha: 330ms p99 is bad. kv miss spike explains memory copies and launch stalls.
praveen: that matches the heuristic we merged last week. It favors the new attn path aggressively and we didn't add any per-stream affinity or debounce. Mixed microbatches cause churn.
ken: hypothesis: microbatch heterogeneity + immediate kernel flip -> kvcache locality broken -> decode tails.
zara: are the swaps happening mid-token or at chunk boundaries?
maria: mid-decode chunk boundaries. the runtime starts decode on kernel A, then when a request's sequence length becomes >140 it switches to kernel B for the remaining tokens. The switch forces KV buffer rebind and a short device-host memcpy for alignment.
liam: mitigation options: 1) enforce per-stream kernel affinity (label streams by initial seq hint), 2) add kernel-debounce/hysteresis, 3) cap microbatch shape to encourage homogenous kernels, 4) speculative kvcache-prefetch for alternate kernel.
sasha: need numbers. what's the throughput cost vs tail benefit?
maria: rough sims from prod-sim:
- cap microbatch to maxTokens=2 -> tokens/s -14%, decode p99 -160ms
- per-stream affinity (sticky) -> tokens/s -5%, decode p99 -95ms
- kernel-debounce 50ms -> tokens/s -3%, decode p99 -110ms
- speculative kvcache-prefetch -> tokens/s -2%, kv-miss-rate down to 0.06 but higher mem footprint
ken: affinity is attractive but risks long-lived affinity causing suboptimal kernel choice if workload shifts mid-request. debounce is simpler and less stateful.
praveen: speculative prefetch is interesting: upon candidate switch detect, async prefetch alt-kv pages into device buffers. Costs memory; could be gated by worker free memory.
liam: can we combine debounce + speculative prefetch selectively? e.g., debounce 30ms + prefetch only when worker mem headroom > X.
maria: yes. I'm proposing an experiment across two arms on canary:
Arm A: microbatch maxTokens=2 (current kernel logic unchanged)
Arm B: keep current maxTokens, enable kernel-debounce=30ms + selective kvcache-prefetch (mem headroom threshold 40%)
measurement: prefill/decode p50/p95/p99, kv-miss-rate, memcpy counts, host-device transfer bytes, CUDA kernel launch latency, tokens/s, CPU spike count
praveen: good. also capture per-request kernel-switch count and time-per-switch. add metrics for kvcache async-prefetch latency.
zara: add trace sampling for top 100 p99 requests and flamegraphs. that'll show where the memcpy and kernel stalls happen.
ken: what success thresholds?
sasha: prefer solution that reduces decode p99 by >=100ms with <8% throughput loss. if Arm B hits that we keep batch shapes.
maria: scheduling: canary pool reserved 2026-03-20T02:00:00Z - 08:00:00Z. plan is A 02:00-04:00, B 04:00-06:00, then buffer analysis.
deploy-bot: canary window booked (maria) 2026-03-20T02:00:00Z, job id: 79245
maria: I'll enable kernel-selection debug and kvcache tracing during the run. will also attach nvprof slices for any sampled p99s.
liam: one more ask: add a short-lived metric: "kernel_switch_memcpy_ops" using perf counter to count memcpy triggers so we can correlate with kv-miss spikes.
praveen: noted. I'll patch the tracer and roll to canary before A starts. :eyes:
ken: if Arm B reduces p99 by ~110ms and tokens/s hit -3..-4% that's my vote. affinity feels heavier operationally.
sasha: agreed. lean towards B if it meets SLO targets.
maria: cool. I'll post experiment doc and links to traces after the run. thanks all. :rocket:
